title: Automated Blendshape Personalization for Faithful Face Animations Using Commodity Smartphones
authors: Timo Menzel, Mario Botsch, Marc Erich Latoschik
venue: ACM Symposium on Virtual Reality Software and Technology
image_caption: Personalized ARKit blendshape mask (left) and full-body avatar with the same expression (right). Lip outlines highlight the accuracy of the transferred personalized blendshapes on the full-body character.
description:
Facial blendshapes are a standard representation for real-time facial animation in games, VR, and digital humans. In practice, however, most character models rely on generic blendshape rigs that fail to capture individual facial characteristics, leading to less convincing animations.
In this project, we present an automated pipeline for generating personalized facial blendshapes from smartphone-captured expressions. Using Apple's ARKit to acquire a set of example facial expressions, we first generate personalized blendshape masks through position-based optimization, and then implant them into realistic full-body characters using seamless partial deformation transfer. The resulting personalized blendshapes significantly improve facial fidelity compared to generic rigs and traditional example-based facial rigging, while requiring only commodity hardware and minimal manual effort.
short_description: A fully automated pipeline for generating high-fidelity, personalized facial blendshapes from smartphone data.

title: Avatars for the Masses: Smartphone-Based Reconstruction of Humans for Virtual Reality
authors: Timo Menzel, Erik Wolf, Stephan Wenninger, Niklas Spinczyk, Lena Holderrieth, Carolin Wienrich, Ulrich Schwanecke, Marc Erich Latoschik, Mario Botsch
image_caption: Avatars for the Masses (A4M) enables non-expert users to create realistic avatars using just their smartphone.
description:
Avatars for the Masses (A4M) is an end-to-end system for reconstructing realistic, VR-ready full-body avatars using commodity smartphones. The system combines a guided mobile capture application with a scalable server-side reconstruction pipeline. Its design enables non-expert users to acquire high-quality scans in uncontrolled, real-world environments.
By integrating guided capture, segmentation, landmark detection, photogrammetry, and template fitting into a fully automated workflow, the system produces high-quality avatars in approximately 20 minutes. Extensive evaluations show that the resulting avatars are comparable in quality to those created with expert-operated scanning setups, demonstrating the feasibility of accessible, large-scale avatar creation.
short_description: An end-to-end smartphone-based pipeline for automated, high-quality full-body avatar reconstruction.

title: Compensating Motion-Induced Errors in Smartphone-Based VR Avatar Reconstruction
authors: Friedemann Runte, Timo Menzel, Ulrich Schwanecke, Mario Botsch
venue: ACM Symposium on Virtual Reality Software and Technology
image_caption: Through sub-scans and silhouette constraints, our method effectively reduces motion artifacts in smartphone-based avatar reconstruction, resulting in more accurate and visually appealing models.
description:
We extend the A4M avatar reconstruction pipeline (Avatars for the Masses) by addressing motion-induced errors that arise during sequential smartphone capture. Even short capture sessions can violate the static-scene assumption of photogrammetry, causing artifacts—particularly in articulated regions such as the arms.
We introduce a sub-scan-based processing strategy that divides image sequences into shorter temporal segments and integrates silhouette constraints and inverse rendering into the reconstruction pipeline. This approach significantly reduces motion artifacts and improves reconstruction accuracy while preserving a simple, user-friendly capture process, making smartphone-based avatar creation more robust under real-world conditions.
short_description: A robust extension of smartphone-based avatar reconstruction that reduces motion artifacts in real-world capture scenarios.
